# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
As originally adopted, the EU AI Act set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI obligations under Annex III [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline) [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113). Following the Commission's "Digital Omnibus on AI," official EU guidance now confirms Annex III high-risk obligations apply from **2 December 2027**, while a separate category tied to Annex I product-safety legislation applies from 2 August 2028 [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force) [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act). A small number of unverified news sources claim a further extension to 2 August 2029, but this is not corroborated by any official EU source, and the source material itself contains an unresolved chronological inconsistency regarding when the Omnibus package was actually adopted.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (as adopted in 2024)
The AI Act as originally adopted set the application date for Annex III high-risk obligations at 2 August 2026, 24 months after the Regulation's entry into force on 1 August 2024 (medium confidence) [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline) [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113). Separately, the European Parliament's own overview describes high-risk obligations as applicable 36 months after entry into force, an inconsistency likely reflecting differing drafting stages (medium confidence) [EU AI Act: first regulation](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence).

### The AI Omnibus and Revised Timeline
The European Commission proposed a "Digital Omnibus on AI" to postpone high-risk rules because harmonised standards and notified bodies were not ready by August 2026 (high confidence) [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act) [Council press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules). Council and Parliament reached political agreement on this simplification package on 7 May 2026 (high confidence) [Council press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules).

**Note on dating inconsistency:** One official source states that "the AI Omnibus/Digital Package on Simplification" was adopted on 19 November 2025 and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) [Regulatory Framework AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai). This adoption date precedes the stated 7 May 2026 political agreement date by nearly six months, which is chronologically contradictory if both refer to the same legislative instrument. The source material does not clarify whether these dates describe two distinct legislative steps (e.g., an earlier, separate simplification package versus the later "AI Omnibus" agreement reached in May 2026) or reflect an error in one of the sources. This inconsistency is treated with caution and flagged further in Contradictions & Uncertainties below.

**Following this amendment, obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems now apply from 2 December 2027** (high confidence), per multiple official EU sources [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation) [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force) [Regulatory Framework AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai). A separate, later deadline of 2 August 2028 applies to high-risk AI systems classified as such because they are safety components or products under Annex I Union harmonisation legislation (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation) [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force).

A specific legal instrument, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, is cited by some sources as the binding text setting the 2 December 2027 date, though this is reported with low confidence given limited sourcing [AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027).

### Distinct Timelines Unaffected by the Delay
Transparency obligations under Article 50 entered into application on 2 August 2026, and prohibitions on non-consensual deepfakes and CSAM-related AI uses applied from 2 December 2026 (high confidence) [Timeline for Implementation](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act). Annex III itself lists categories of use cases that *may* be classified as high-risk, rather than systems automatically deemed high-risk (low confidence) [Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
**Adoption vs. agreement date conflict:** The source material states the simplification package was "adopted" on 19 November 2025 while political agreement between Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026 — an adoption date preceding the agreement date, which is chronologically implausible for a single legislative instrument [Regulatory Framework AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai) vs. [Council press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules). This may reflect two distinct legislative steps or packages, or an error in one source; it should be treated with caution pending clarification of which specific instrument each date refers to.

Official EU guidance is also internally inconsistent: the Article 111 guidance page still references 2 August 2026 as a trigger date for legacy systems, while other official pages state 2 December 2027 is now the operative Annex III date — likely an unupdated guidance page rather than substantive conflict [Article 111 guidance](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111) vs. [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation).

Three news/blog sources (flagged low confidence, below 0.4) claim a further extension to 2 August 2029 following an alleged "second amendment" in September 2026 [EU AI Act legal guide](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update); this is **not corroborated by any official EU source** and should be treated with significant skepticism pending verification.

Numerous pre-Omnibus commentary sources continue to cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline, reflecting outdated information superseded by the Omnibus's entry into force (low confidence) [CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20).

## Knowledge Gaps
- Whether the 19 November 2025 "adoption" and 7 May 2026 "agreement" dates refer to the same or different legislative instruments.
- Whether the EUR-Lex consolidated text (dated 27.07.2026) has been fully updated throughout to reflect 2 December 2027.
- Whether the 2 August 2029 date has any basis in an actual adopted amendment, or is erroneous reporting.
- Whether further conditions could still alter the 2 December 2027 date.
- The precise legal status of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 relative to any subsequent amending instruments.

4. [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
As originally adopted, the EU AI Act set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI obligations under Annex III [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline) [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113). However, following the Commission's "Digital Omnibus on AI" and political agreement between Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, this deadline was extended: official EU guidance now confirms Annex III high-risk obligations apply from **2 December 2027**, while a separate category tied to Annex I product-safety legislation applies from 2 August 2028 [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force) [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act). A small number of unverified news sources claim a further extension to 2 August 2029, but this is not corroborated by any official EU source.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (as adopted in 2024)
The AI Act as originally adopted set the application date for Annex III high-risk obligations at 2 August 2026, 24 months after the Regulation's entry into force on 1 August 2024 (medium confidence) [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline) [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113). Separately, the European Parliament's own overview describes high-risk obligations as applicable 36 months after entry into force, an inconsistency likely reflecting differing drafting stages (medium confidence) [EU AI Act: first regulation](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence).

### The AI Omnibus and Revised Timeline
The European Commission proposed a "Digital Omnibus on AI" to postpone high-risk rules because harmonised standards and notified bodies were not ready by August 2026 (high confidence) [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act) [Council press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules). Council and Parliament reached political agreement on this simplification package on 7 May 2026 (high confidence) [Council press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules). The package was adopted on 19 November 2025 and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) [Regulatory Framework AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai).

**Following this amendment, obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems now apply from 2 December 2027** (high confidence), per multiple official EU sources [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation) [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force) [Regulatory Framework AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai). A separate, later deadline of 2 August 2028 applies to high-risk AI systems classified as such because they are safety components or products under Annex I Union harmonisation legislation (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation) [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force).

A specific legal instrument, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, is cited by some sources as the binding text setting the 2 December 2027 date, though this is reported with low confidence given limited sourcing [AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027).

### Distinct Timelines Unaffected by the Delay
Separately from the Annex III high-risk timeline, transparency obligations under Article 50 entered into application on 2 August 2026, and prohibitions on non-consensual deepfakes and CSAM-related AI uses applied from 2 December 2026 (high confidence) [Timeline for Implementation](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act). Annex III itself lists categories of use cases that *may* be classified as high-risk, rather than systems automatically deemed high-risk (low confidence) [Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Official EU guidance is internally inconsistent: the Article 111 guidance page still references 2 August 2026 as a trigger date for legacy systems, while other official pages state 2 December 2027 is now the operative Annex III date — likely an unupdated guidance page rather than substantive conflict [Article 111 guidance](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111) vs. [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation).

Three news/blog sources (flagged low confidence, below 0.4) claim a further extension to 2 August 2029 following an alleged "second amendment" in September 2026 [EU AI Act legal guide](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update); this is **not corroborated by any official EU source** and should be treated with significant skepticism pending verification.

Numerous pre-Omnibus commentary sources continue to cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline, reflecting outdated information superseded by the Omnibus's entry into force (low confidence) [CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20).

## Knowledge Gaps
- Whether the EUR-Lex consolidated text (dated 27.07.2026) has been fully updated throughout to reflect 2 December 2027.
- Whether the 2 August 2029 date has any basis in an actual adopted amendment, or is erroneous reporting.
- Whether further conditions (e.g., Commission confirmation of standards readiness) could still alter the 2 December 2027 date.
- The precise legal status and scope of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 relative to any subsequent amending instruments.
